patients.summary: Healthy university student who joined the practice at 21 and lives with his parents in Amherst. Schizophrenia was diagnosed by psychiatry in October 2024 after months of withdrawal and then paranoid delusions; he declined medication until a February 2026 ED visit and inpatient psychiatric stay started risperidone. The practice follows him with antipsychotic metabolic monitoring.

documents.title: New patient request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Mother called on behalf of her son Ethan, 21, who has outgrown his pediatrician and needs an adult doctor before he heads back to classes. No current concerns per mom. Insured through his parents' PPO. Booked new patient physical 8/22 at 9:00. Asked mom to have the pediatric office send his records and vaccine history.

documents.title: Pediatric practice records
documents.author: pediatrics
documents.body:
Records from his pediatric practice, 22 pages, covering well visits from infancy through age 19. Growth and development normal throughout. No chronic problems, no hospitalizations, no surgeries. No known drug allergies. Childhood and adolescent immunization series complete, including Tdap at age 11 and the adolescent series; influenza most years. Last well visit at 19 unremarkable.

Filed to media. Immunization dates abstracted for the new patient visit.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
21 y/o M establishing care, coming over from his pediatrician. Rising junior at the university, commutes from home, lives with mom and dad in Amherst. Feels well. No complaints today.

PMH: none. PSH: none. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: maternal uncle with schizophrenia; paternal grandmother with bipolar disorder; mother with major depression.
SH: never a smoker, does not drink. Tried cannabis in the past, not using now. Not sexually active currently; discussed HIV/HCV one-time screening, agrees.

ROS: negative except as above. Sleeping fine, mood good.

Exam: well-appearing young man, pleasant, good eye contact. HEENT normal, TMs clear. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement or nodes. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin without rashes. Neuro grossly intact, normal gait.
PHQ-9 2.

A/P
1. Health maintenance in a healthy 21 y/o. Pediatric records reviewed; series complete, last Tdap at 11, so Tdap given today. HIV and hep C screening drawn. Flu and COVID in October, nurse visit.
2. Family psychiatric history noted. Asked him to reach out if sleep, mood or stress change during the semester.
Return yearly.

documents.title: Your screening results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Ethan, your HIV and hepatitis C screens came back negative, which is what we expected. Nothing else to do on these. Good luck with the fall semester.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for seasonal vaccines between classes. Screening questions negative, no prior reactions. Flu 0.5 mL IM left arm, COVID 2023-24 formula 0.3 mL IM right arm, VIS provided for both. Observed 15 minutes, no reaction, left feeling fine.

documents.title: We missed you on Tuesday
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Ethan, we had you down for your yearly physical on 7/23 at 10:30 and didn't see you. No problem, these things happen. Reply here or call and we'll find a new time that works around your summer.

documents.title: Parent concern
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Mother called. Since around spring Ethan has been keeping to his room, stopped seeing his friends, skips family meals. She and his dad have heard him talking out loud when nobody is with him and laughing to himself. No threats, no talk of hurting himself per mom, eating, no known substance use. He agreed to come in if they come with him. Discussed with PCP: 40 min slot Tues 9/24, earlier if things change; ED or 988 for any safety concern. Mom verbalized understanding.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: five months of social withdrawal, talking and laughing to himself

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with both parents, who did most of the talking. Last seen at his new patient visit a year ago; missed his July physical.

Parents describe roughly five months of Ethan drawing inward: in his room most of the day, little interest in friends or in family, and they hear him talking to himself and laughing at nothing in particular. They are not aware of drug use. Ethan himself says he is "fine," that he just likes being alone. Answers are short. Denies feeling sad or down. Denies any thoughts of hurting himself or anyone else. Will not elaborate on what he is talking about when alone. Sleeping and eating per parents.

Meds none. NKDA. FH notable for schizophrenia in a maternal uncle, bipolar disorder in paternal grandmother, depression in mother. Tried cannabis years ago, says none now.

Exam: vitals reviewed, unremarkable. Quiet, flat, limited eye contact, slightly unkempt. No tremor. Heart and lungs normal. Neuro: CN II-XII intact, strength and reflexes symmetric, gait steady, no focal findings.
PHQ-9 3.

A/P
Behavior change over five months in a 23 y/o with a strong family psychiatric history. Not acutely unsafe today by his report and parents'. Want a medical screen and psychiatry soon.
- CBC, CMP, TSH today
- Urgent referral to outpatient psychiatry, parents will keep after the scheduling
- Safety plan reviewed with parents: ED or 988 if he talks about harming himself or others, or stops eating or sleeping
Follow up after psychiatry.

documents.title: Bloodwork and psychiatry appointment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Ethan, your blood count, chemistries and thyroid all came back normal. The psychiatry office has you for Wednesday 10/16. Please keep that appointment, and it's fine for your mom or dad to come with you. Call us if anything changes before then.

procedures.procedure: Psychiatric diagnostic evaluation with medical services

documents.title: Psychiatry evaluation letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outside psychiatry practice. Visit of 10/16/2024.

Thank you for sending Ethan, 23, whom we saw with his mother and father. They describe half a year of growing isolation; he keeps to his room, has little to do with friends or family, and is overheard speaking to no one and laughing without a clear cause. He used cannabis in the past and says not lately.

Allergies: NKDA. Medications: none.
Family: schizophrenia in a maternal uncle, bipolar illness in the paternal grandmother, major depression in his mother.

Vitals normal. He was unkempt, made little eye contact, spoke in a flat tone with sparse replies. Described his mood as fine and denied sadness or loss of enjoyment. No suicidal or homicidal ideation. Thinking was hard to follow and he seemed absorbed in his own thoughts. Neurological screen normal.

Impression: schizophrenia. We discussed starting an antipsychotic. Ethan does not see himself as ill and declined; his parents would like him to start but respect his choice for now. Psychoeducation given to the family. We will continue to follow him in clinic and revisit medication at each visit.

Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Flu season reminder
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Our records show you haven't had a flu shot this season. Walk-in nurse hours are weekday afternoons, or let us know if you got one somewhere else.

documents.title: Update on Ethan
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is Ethan's dad writing on his account. I took him back to psychiatry on Thursday. He hasn't been going to class at all this semester, and now he's convinced the neighbors put cameras in our house and that the TV is sending him messages. They again suggested medication and he said no. He's going to take a medical leave from school and psychiatry is doing the paperwork for the dean's office. I don't think there's anything you need to do, I just wanted his regular doctor to know where things stand.

documents.title: RE: Update on Ethan
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me, I'm glad he's still connected with psychiatry. If his school or insurance needs anything from our office for the leave, send it over. And if he ever says anything about harming himself or someone else, go straight to the ED or call 988.

documents.title: Psychiatry follow-up note
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Psychiatry follow-up, 02/20/2025. Seen with father about four months after his initial evaluation in October 2024.

Symptoms now ten months in duration. He has withdrawn further and stopped going to his university classes. He holds the belief that neighbors installed hidden cameras in the family home to watch him and that television broadcasts carry messages meant for him. Still talks and laughs to himself alone in his room. No alcohol, no drug use. Denies mood symptoms.

Dx: schizophrenia. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.

Plan: antipsychotic again recommended; he declines. Supported medical leave from the university, letter provided. Family to call with any safety concern. Return 6-8 weeks.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Mother drove him and sat in for part of the visit.

On medical leave from the university since the spring. Still seeing outpatient psychiatry every couple of months for schizophrenia. Has not wanted to take medication; psychiatry continues to offer it. Ethan says things are "okay," spends most of the day at home. No physical complaints. Denies sadness, denies thoughts of harming himself or others. No alcohol, no cannabis, never smoked.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: guarded, brief answers, appropriately groomed today. Vitals fine, weight steady. HEENT normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Skin clear. Neuro nonfocal.
PHQ-9 3.

A/P
1. Schizophrenia, followed by psychiatry, untreated by his choice. No safety concerns today. Mom knows to call.
2. Health maintenance: HIV/HCV done 2023, Tdap 2023. He'd rather come back for flu and COVID once the new vaccines are in; nurse visit in October.
Yearly, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came in with father. Vaccine screening negative. Influenza 2025-26 0.5 mL IM L arm; COVID 2025-26 0.5 mL IM R arm. VIS given. Quiet, cooperative. Sat 15 min with dad, no reaction.

reports.text: Noncontrast axial images of the head. No intracranial hemorrhage, mass, mass effect or midline shift. Gray-white differentiation preserved. Ventricles and sulci normal for age. Basal cisterns patent. Calvarium intact. Visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoids clear.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

events.reason: Mother reports ED visit and admission

documents.title: Family call: hospitalized
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Mom called to let us know Ethan was taken to the ED Sunday by her and his father after two weeks of hearing voices and acting erratically, increasingly afraid the neighbors were plotting against him. He was admitted to the inpatient psychiatric unit at the regional hospital and agreed to stay. She expects he'll be there about a week or more. Told her PCP will be updated and we'd like to see him after discharge; she'll call when he's home. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: PCP review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Noted. Please book a post-discharge visit within 1-2 weeks of his return and request the ED record and discharge summary.

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED encounter 2/22/2026. 24M with schizophrenia, untreated, followed by outpatient psychiatry since 10/2024. Parents brought him for 2 wk of erratic behavior and auditory hallucinations; talking to himself, appears to respond to voices, increasingly paranoid that neighbors are conspiring to harm him. Home meds: none. NKDA. FH: schizophrenia (maternal uncle), bipolar (paternal grandmother), MDD (mother). Never smoker, no EtOH, on medical leave from university.

VS WNL. Disheveled, poor eye contact, internally preoccupied. Medically: CBC, CMP and urine tox unremarkable. Head CT without contrast negative.

Impression: acute exacerbation of psychosis, schizophrenia.
Dispo: evaluated by psychiatry in the ED; voluntary admission to inpatient psychiatry.

documents.title: External fill history
documents.author: MA
documents.body: External fill history pulled for med rec ahead of post-discharge visit: risperidone 2 mg tab, #30, 1 at bedtime, filled 3/4/2026, prescriber inpatient psychiatry. No other fills in the past 12 months.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Spoke with mom. Ethan discharged home yesterday on risperidone 2 mg at night. First outpatient psychiatry appointment is next week. Booked with PCP Thu 3/12 at 10:20; asked them to come fasting for blood work and to bring the discharge paperwork. No acute concerns.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth at bedtime

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen with his mother, 8 days after discharge from inpatient psychiatry (2/22 to 3/4), admitted through the ED for two weeks of voices and paranoia about the neighbors. Discharge paperwork not brought; we have the ED note and a fill history. Records request out for the discharge summary.

Started risperidone in hospital and went home on 2 mg at bedtime. Mom gives it to him nightly, no missed doses. He says the voices are "quieter." Has his first outpatient psychiatry appointment this coming Monday. Denies thoughts of harming himself or others. Sleeping. Eating as usual.

Meds: risperidone 2 mg qhs (psychiatry). NKDA.

Exam: calm, cooperative, sparse speech, fair eye contact. Vitals normal, weight unchanged from fall. Heart regular, lungs clear. No tremor or rigidity, gait normal.

A/P
1. Schizophrenia, recent hospitalization, now on risperidone through psychiatry. Added to med list as psychiatry-prescribed; psychiatry will manage dose and refills.
2. Antipsychotic monitoring: baseline fasting lipids and A1c today; weight and BP at each visit.
Recheck in about a month.

documents.title: Blood work results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Ethan, your cholesterol panel, fasting sugar and A1c from yesterday are all normal. These give us a starting point now that you're on risperidone, and we'll repeat them in a few months. See you in April.

documents.title: Records request sent
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Release signed by patient at 3/12 visit. Request faxed to the regional hospital health information office for the inpatient psychiatry discharge summary, admission 2/22/2026 to 3/4/2026. Will follow up if not received in 2 weeks.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

orders.reason: antipsychotic metabolic monitoring at about three months
antipsychotic metabolic monitoring at about three months

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u, came on his own today (dad waiting in the car).

Now about 7 weeks on risperidone 2 mg at night. Has seen outpatient psychiatry twice since discharge, they are keeping the same dose. Taking it every night. Says he feels "more settled" and the voices come less often. Still on leave from school, not thinking about the fall yet. No thoughts of harming self or others.

Meds: risperidone 2 mg qhs (psychiatry). NKDA.

Exam: calm, more conversational than last visit. Vitals normal, weight stable. No tremor, normal gait.

A/P
1. Schizophrenia on risperidone per psychiatry, improving by his report.
2. Metabolic monitoring: baseline labs normal in March. Ordered repeat fasting lipids and A1c for June, around 3 months on the drug; lab is walk-in.
Next routine visit in the fall, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Inpatient psychiatry discharge summary
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Inpatient psychiatry, admitted 2/22/2026 from the ED, discharged 3/4/2026.

Reason for admission: two weeks of auditory hallucinations, erratic behavior and paranoid ideation about neighbors in a 24-year-old man with schizophrenia diagnosed in 10/2024, never treated with medication. Voluntary.
Medical workup in the ED (CBC, CMP, urine tox, noncontrast head CT) unremarkable.

Course: agreed to a trial of risperidone, titrated to 2 mg at bedtime and tolerated without notable side effects. Hallucinations lessened and paranoia less prominent by discharge. No aggression on the unit. Denied suicidal or homicidal ideation throughout.

Discharge medication: risperidone 2 mg PO at bedtime.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: outpatient psychiatry within two weeks; primary care.
Discharge diagnosis: schizophrenia.

documents.title: June blood work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Ethan, the repeat cholesterol and sugar tests are normal again, no change from March. Nothing to do. We'll keep checking these about once a year while you're on risperidone.

documents.title: Outpatient psychiatry note
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body: Outpatient psychiatry, visit 6/29/2026. Schizophrenia, here with father for medication follow-up four months after inpatient discharge. Continues risperidone 2 mg nightly with good adherence. Remains on medical leave from the university. No SI/HI. Allergies NKDA. Plan: continue risperidone 2 mg qhs, return 8 weeks. Copy to PCP.

documents.title: September appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, this is Ethan's mom. Can you confirm he's on the schedule in September? I have the 24th written down but want to make sure.

documents.title: RE: September appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Yes, Thursday 9/24 at 10:40 with his doctor. See you then.
